s1.syndrome_frame: subacute, multifocal, pruritic, painful skin eruption
salient_findings: well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the abdomen, axillae, and inguinal folds
scattered erythematous scaly papules and plaques on the scalp, extremities, and hands
confluent erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques with plate-like scales on the plantar feet
key_facts: 12-year history of recurrent follicular lymphoma
subacute onset of skin eruption
pruritic and painful skin lesions
skin eruption began on the abdomen and then involved the scalp, groin, and extremities
denied fevers, chills, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms
medications included oxycodone, duvelisib, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
medications started 14 months earlier for lymphoma management
skin biopsies showed parakeratosis with collections of neutrophils and dermal eosinophils
skin biopsies showed regular epidermal hyperplasia with elongated rete ridges and thin suprapapillary plates

shortlist.label: Drug-induced psoriasiform eruption
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsies showed parakeratosis with collections of neutrophils and dermal eosinophils, consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction, and patient recently started duvelisib

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions described as well-demarcated erythematous plaques with plate-like scales, consistent with psoriasis, but less likely given recent medication changes

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions described as erythematous scaly papules and plaques, but less likely given lack of characteristic palmoplantar keratoderma and orange-red hue

shortlist.label: Seborrheic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions described as erythematous plaques on the abdomen and axillae, but less likely given presence of pruritus and painful lesions

shortlist.label: Atopic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: patient presents with pruritic and painful skin lesions, but less likely given lack of personal or family history of atopy

shortlist.label: Contact dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions described as well-demarcated erythematous plaques, but less likely given lack of clear exposure history

shortlist.label: Guttate psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions described as scattered erythematous scaly papules and plaques, but less likely given lack of characteristic small, droplike lesions

shortlist.label: Inverse psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions described as well-demarcated erythematous plaques in intertriginous areas, but less likely given presence of scaling and less typical location

raw.rationale: The patient's skin eruption began after starting new medications, including duvelisib, and skin biopsies showed findings consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction, such as parakeratosis and dermal eosinophils.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: Lack of prior history of psoriasis and temporal association with new medication use

rejected.why: Distribution of skin lesions and biopsy findings are not typical for seborrheic dermatitis
